claim: Late-VOC systematic cinnamon cultivation was centred in the low-country coastal belt around Colombo and related maritime districts, whereas the nineteenth-century British coffee boom expanded primarily into the central Kandyan highlands after 1815; tea then reused much of the coffee highland estate and transport system. The long-run continuity from cinnamon to coffee/tea is therefore export-institutional and macroeconomic rather than a direct reuse of the same plantation lands.
bounded_by: RUN44 did not trace every named cinnamon parcel through British 1796–1830s land records. The evidence strongly supports a coastal-cinnamon versus Kandyan-highland coffee/tea spatial discontinuity, but confidence A requires direct cadastral/deed comparison. Do not claim that no former cinnamon land ever entered later plantation uses.
notes: Closes Q-R43-CINNAMON-TO-COFFEE-TEA-CONTINUITY-001 at bounded confidence. Narrative payoff: 1815 changes not only sovereignty but the economic geography available to colonial plantation capital.
